skeptic.objection: Lot 2 does not look like a free-standing remainder: it looks like the planned expansion and stormwater corner of the 907,665 SF Lot 1 building next door. The developer's own brochure for that building advertises trailer storage of 161 spaces expandable to 477, and its site-plan drawing (an image, not quotable) puts 220 of those future trailer spaces, plus a detention pond, in the triangle between Oakley Industrial Blvd and Creekwood Rd, which is the shape and position of this 20.4-acre lot on the county parcel map. On the county map the Oakley Industrial Blvd road bed along Lot 2 lies inside Lot 1's tax parcel, and the county street layer shows that segment with no ownership value, created in February 2026. That leaves Creekwood Rd as Lot 2's only certain public frontage. Creekwood Rd is a 24 ft local road, and the houses on its other side face the lot. Nothing here proves an easement, option or expansion right over Lot 2, so the lead is weakened, not killed. Title must settle that before anyone approaches the owner.

claims.text: The developer's brochure for the Lot 1 building at 1625 Oakley Industrial Blvd (linked from Red Rock's current Shugart Farms page) advertises its trailer storage as 161 spaces, expandable to 477. Its site-plan drawing (image only) labels the extra spaces as future trailer spaces, 220 of them in the north triangle between Oakley Industrial Blvd and Creekwood Rd. By its shape and position on the county parcel map, that triangle is this Lot 2. The link from the quote to Lot 2 is the skeptic's reading of the drawing, not text.
claims.quote: Trailer storage 161 (12’ x 60’) storage spaces (Expandable to 477)

claims.text: The same brochure lists site works already built for future expansion around the Lot 1 building: a future loop road graded with the storm drainage in place.

claims.text: Fulton County's parcel layer was asked which parcel contains the point -84.60402, 33.53109. By the county street layer, that point is on the Oakley Industrial Blvd centreline, about 8 m north-west of Lot 2's north-west line. The layer answers Lot 1 (07 390001641430), so on the county tax map the road bed beside Lot 2 lies inside Lot 1's parcel and not in a separate right-of-way. That parcel is held in the Development Authority's name (the bond-lease title), with the tax bill going to a Dallas address.

Fulton County's street centreline layer (FultonStreetBaseMap layer 147) was asked for streets within 60 ft of Lot 2's own polygon. Its Oakley Industrial Blvd segment along Lot 2's north-west side (address range 1625 to 1625, subdivision 'Project Miles', the developer's code name for the Lot 1 building, created 2026-02-19 by its CreateDate) has no Ownership value and is classed Local - Residential, while the older Oakley segment and Creekwood Rd are recorded as Public. Whether this stretch is dedicated public right-of-way that gives Lot 2 frontage is not shown.

The same answer gives Creekwood Rd, which runs along Lot 2's east side, as a public local road 24 ft wide with 2 lanes and a 35 mph limit. Its centreline is digitised north to south and lies east of Lot 2, so its left-side (east) address range is 8400 to 8488, in ZIP 30268. That range takes in the homesteaded house at 8468 Creekwood reported in plans-4 and plans-5, which therefore sits across this road from Lot 2. Lot 2's screener frontage of about 1,369 ft matches the length of this east side, not the Oakley side.

open_items: Seen, not verifiable as text: page 2 of the brochure has a site-plan image. It labels (220) FUTURE TRAILER SPACES in the north triangle between Oakley Industrial Blvd and Creekwood Rd, plus (40) future trailer spaces and (56) future trailer storage. Existing storage is (90) plus (71), which gives 161 built and 316 future, adding up to the 477 in the text. It also shows a stormwater detention pond near Creekwood Rd that, scaled against the county parcel polygons, appears to fall inside Lot 2. Ask title for any stormwater, drainage, access or parking easement, option, right of first refusal or tenant expansion right over Lot 2 in favour of the Lot 1 owner or tenant.

Market verdict: market-1 shows the JV's 2019 bond for the Lot 1 building, not any plan for Lot 2. The better reading of the evidence may be that Lot 2 is held back for the Lot 1 building (trailer and stormwater use) rather than pursued as a separate project. Either way, a sale may need the consent of, or carry obligations to, the Lot 1 owner.

Ask Fairburn and title whether the Oakley Industrial Blvd segment along Lot 2 (county street layer, created Feb 2026, no ownership value) is dedicated public right-of-way. If it is not, truck access to Lot 2 would be only from Creekwood Rd, a 24 ft local road with homes on the opposite side, or over Lot 1. The adopted plan (plans-4) asks for direct truck-route access and no adjacency to residential neighbourhoods.

Creekwood Rd's east side carries ZIP 30268 (Palmetto) in the county street layer. Confirm which jurisdiction and zoning govern the houses across the road, and what M-1 buffer or setback applies against them.

Search results (snippets only, not read): LXP Industrial's 2021 report lists 1625 Oakley Industrial Blvd (Lot 1), and a July 2026 item reports a Brookfield and CPP Investments deal to acquire LXP. If accurate, the Lot 1 owner is an institutional landlord that may want Lot 2 for its building. Not verified.

Fairburn's '2025 Comprehensive Plan Update' page says that process was expected to finish by October 2025. Confirm that the plan the first pass quoted (DocumentCenter View 2932) is the currently adopted version, and check its future development map at parcel scale.

The county Structures layer query returned an error, so whether any structure, pavement or pond has been built on Lot 2 since the 2021 brochure was not checked. The county roll (market-3) shows no improvements assessed. Drive the site or look at current aerials.
